decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 summarizes organization only as “easy to organize and search.” Client entry 4 adds the missing behavior: “having the app suggest tags I've already used.”
decisions.note: Corrective extension during requirements framing: existing-tag autocomplete was absent from the presented organization behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 presents generic organization. Client entry 4 explicitly adds “being able to jump to just one tag's links.”
decisions.note: Corrective extension during requirements framing: the client restores the reference requirement for filtering by a selected tag.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 presents saving from “a prominent address box at the top”; client entry 8 confirms “a clear address box up top where I paste a link.”
decisions.note: Conforming prototype decision: a bookmark is saved by entering its URL.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 specifies automatic presentation of “title, short description, and website.” Client entry 8 approves the title, description, and site without mentioning the omitted favicon or preview image; entries 83–84 settle this scope.
decisions.note: Prototype-to-specification divergence: automatic metadata is scoped to title/description/site, omitting the required favicon and preview image.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 defines each card as showing title, description, and website; entry 17/round 9 later adds tags beneath it. Clients entries 8 and 18 approve those fields without requesting the required favicon.
decisions.note: Prototype divergence: the settled readable card exposes title, description, site, and tags but no favicon.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 has the user click Save before collected details appear; entry 11/round 6 says correction starts from the saved bookmark's “Edit details” control. Client entries 8 and 12 accept that flow without requesting ordinary pre-save editing.
decisions.note: Prototype divergence: collected title/description can be corrected after saving, but the presented normal save flow omits editing them before saving.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7 demonstrates replacing a saved description and selecting Save changes; client entry 14 confirms the corrected description returns on the bookmark.
decisions.note: Conforming prototype decision for post-save title/description editing.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 11/round 6 limits the editor to title and description. Client entry 12 states the expectation to “fix the actual link itself” but permits deferral. Maker entries 81 and 83 retain address correction as later-cycle work; client entries 82 and 84 explicitly accept that, saying it is “fine” and they are “comfortable” with it.
decisions.note: One linked clarification and disposition, counted once: the client explicitly identifies URL editing as expected but accepts its omission from this cycle at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 17/round 9 offers alternatives including Version B's fixed tag chips, which lacks type-ahead autocomplete. Client entry 18 selects Version A and explains, “I'd want the type-to-find as the collection grows.”
decisions.note: Corrective selection during prototype review: offered alternatives differed in REF-BM-10 fulfillment, and the client selected a conforming autocomplete flow.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 19/round 10 demonstrates typing “rec,” selecting the existing Recipes suggestion, and attaching it; client entry 20 confirms that exact completion.
decisions.note: Conforming revised prototype decision for assigning an existing tag through autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 23/round 12 presents controls that show only Recipes bookmarks and display the active tag and count; client entry 24 selects the sidebar and confirms the two matching results.
decisions.note: Conforming revised prototype decision for filtering by a specific tag; sidebar versus dropdown/chip is an orthogonal UI preference.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 27, 29, and 31/rounds 14–16 test note, title, and description matches; entry 33 summarizes the settled scope as search across “titles, descriptions, and your notes.” Client entry 34 approves that scope without mentioning URL search.
decisions.note: Prototype/specification divergence: full-text search omits the bookmark URL.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 29/round 15 searches lowercase “weeknights” and matches the title “Quick Tomato Pasta for Weeknights”; client entry 30 confirms the match.
decisions.note: Conforming prototype decision demonstrating case-insensitive search.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 35/round 18 presents marking The Food Lab for Read later while retaining it in the main library; client entry 36 selects the labeled control and approves that flag behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming prototype decision for marking a bookmark unread/read-later.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 37/round 19 presents a dedicated Read later view containing only The Food Lab; client entry 38 confirms this is the expected waiting-items view.
decisions.note: Conforming prototype decision for a separate unread-bookmarks view.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 39 and 41/rounds 20–21 show Mark as read removing the item from Read later while retaining it in All bookmarks. Client entries 40 and 42 confirm that only the waiting flag is cleared.
decisions.note: Conforming prototype decision for marking an item read without deleting it.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 45/round 23 presents selecting the full bookmark card to open the original page; client entry 46 confirms it reaches the saved page.
decisions.note: Conforming prototype decision; opening in a new tab and making the whole card clickable are functionally equivalent UI choices.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 53/round 27 warns that the URL is already saved and returns the user to the existing bookmark rather than creating another. Client entry 54 confirms “I end up back at the existing bookmark rather than cluttering things with duplicates.”
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-save decision: it converges on the existing editable bookmark and prevents a duplicate.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 57/round 29 presents explicitly creating and attaching Travel when no existing tag matches; client entry 58 approves creating and adding it in place.
decisions.note: Conforming prototype decision for assigning a newly created tag.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 67–71/rounds 34–36 settle notes as a text field shown beneath the bookmark, editable, and searchable. Client entries 68–72 approve those behaviors but neither presentation nor response includes markdown input or rendered markdown; entry 83 closes the note scope.
decisions.note: Prototype-to-specification divergence: personal notes are specified as visible searchable text, omitting the required markdown authoring/rendering behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 71/round 36 includes “editing it later” in the settled note flow; client entry 72 expressly confirms the note can be edited later.
decisions.note: Conforming prototype decision for editing a bookmark's note after saving.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 73/round 37 blocks saving an empty title and states “titles may not” be empty. Client entry 74 endorses that assumption but does not identify that the reference makes only URL mandatory.
decisions.note: Prototype divergence: the editor imposes a required-title constraint beyond the reference's URL-only required-field rule. Approval does not demonstrate awareness of that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker entries 77 and 79/rounds 39–40 present compact title/description/note snippets with Show full bookmark and all tags wrapped visibly; client entries 78 and 80 select and approve that readable expandable treatment.
decisions.note: Conforming readability decision; truncation with an expansion control is functionally equivalent and the tags remain exposed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 81/round 41 proposes that when a source changes or disappears, Keepwell preserves only bookmark details and retries the stored address even if the site errors. Client entry 82 approves preserving metadata and trying the broken destination; entries 83–84 settle this as “preservation when source websites fail” without a local HTML/PDF snapshot.
decisions.note: Late prototype/specification divergence: failure resilience preserves bookmark metadata but omits the required local page snapshot and PDF-download rule.
